title: Iron, Steel & Aluminium — DPP characteristics
description: Field specifications for the Iron, Steel & Aluminium Digital Product Passport, shaped for UNTP's credentialSubject.characteristics extension point. Economic operators and facility identifiers are carried by the UNTP envelope and are deliberately absent here.

gtin.title: GTIN
gtin.description: GTIN-14 product identifier (14-digit Global Trade Item Number).
gtin.x-citationNote: ESPR 32024R1781 mandates no product data of its own. Art. 7(1) makes information requirements those 'laid down in the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4'; Art. 9(2) says those acts 'shall … specify' what a passport carries; and Art. 27 binds manufacturers only 'when placing products COVERED BY a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4' on the market. All three defer to an Art. 4 act, and none is adopted for this category — so this field is anticipated, not required. Verified against the EUR-Lex text. Reference: GS1.

cbamAccountNumber.x-citationNote: The CBAM registry account belongs to the authorised declarant — the importer. Nothing requires a producer to publish it, and it identifies a party rather than a product.

ceMarking.title: CE Marking
ceMarking.description: Whether the CE marking is affixed. Under the CPR it applies only where a harmonised technical specification or European Technical Assessment covers the product (e.g. structural steelwork under EN 1090-1); mill products not so covered cannot be CE-marked.
ceMarking.x-provision: Arts. 13(1), 17-18; Art. 94 (Reg. (EU) 305/2011 Arts. 4-9 continue to apply until 8 Jan 2040 for products under harmonised standards cited under it)
ceMarking.x-citationNote: CE marking under the CPR is conditional: it applies only where a harmonised technical specification or European Technical Assessment covers the product, and a product covered by neither cannot be CE-marked at all. For steel this is the sub-case — structural steelwork under a harmonised standard (EN 1090-1) is covered; mill products and much rebar are not.

declarationOfPerformanceUri.x-citationNote: Under the CPR a Declaration of Performance is required where a harmonised technical specification or a European Technical Assessment covers the product, and the duty is to DRAW IT UP and supply it. Steel structural products can fall in scope; publishing a link supports that duty without replacing it, and the CPR passport itself is deferred pending the Art. 75(1) delegated act.

ceMarkingStatus.title: CE Marking Status
ceMarkingStatus.description: Whether the product bears CE marking and its validity
ceMarkingStatus.x-provision: Arts. 13(1), 17-18; Art. 94 (Reg. (EU) 305/2011 Arts. 4-9 continue to apply until 8 Jan 2040 for products under harmonised standards cited under it)
ceMarkingStatus.x-citationNote: CE marking under the CPR is CONDITIONAL: it applies only where a harmonised technical specification or European Technical Assessment covers the product, and a product covered by neither cannot be CE-marked at all. For steel this is the sub-case — structural steelwork under a harmonised standard (paradigm EN 1090-1) is covered; mill products and much rebar are not. Never model steel as always-CE or never-CE, which is why not_applicable is an enum member and why the field cannot be required.
